canonicalDecimalString.description: Exact canonical decimal: no exponent, leading plus, unnecessary integer leading zero, trailing fractional zero, trailing decimal point, or negative zero.

statusEvent.description: Append-only transition evidence only. This generic event cannot itself authorize or block governed downstream use; the applicable typed human decision record is required.

provenanceRecord.description: Operational provenance only; this record cannot confer governed approval or downstream eligibility.

When sourceQuarantineDecisionId is non-null it resolves to exactly one prior quarantine decision whose recomputed decisionContentSha256 equals sourceQuarantineDecisionContentSha256, whose artifactSha256 matches exactly, and whose effective state permits the requested transition; both source fields are null only when no quarantine decision is applicable
Replay is human-only, gapless, non-branching, same-artifact, and independent of timestamps
Approval of an artifact subject to quarantine requires an effective same-artifact human release decision through sourceQuarantineDecisionId

inherit-approval is initial ordinal 1 with no eligibility-chain predecessor; it derives eligibility solely from the separate current-effective typed quarantine release identified operationally by sourceQuarantineDecisionId and deterministically by sourceQuarantineDecisionContentSha256 for the same exact bytes
Effective eligibility exists only when replay ends in eligible and every applicable quarantine/release decision remains effective
ClassificationProposal remains proposed or unresolved and is never mutated by review

terminalDispositionLedger contains exactly discoveredRecordTotal entries and each recordId occurs exactly once

sourceArtifacts plus extractedMembers equals discoveredRecordTotal and agrees with originLedger category counts

x-numeric-canonicalization.jsonNumbers: All finite deterministic JSON numbers use RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme serialization over representable IEEE-754 binary64 values. Equivalent notation such as 1, 1.0, and 1e0 produces identical bytes; negative zero serializes as 0; NaN and positive or negative infinity are invalid; source-language number lexemes are never hashed.
x-numeric-canonicalization.exactDecimals: Any decimal whose lexical precision is material is encoded as canonicalDecimalString, not a JSON number. The grammar prohibits exponent notation, leading plus, unnecessary integer leading zero, unnecessary trailing fractional zero, trailing decimal point, and negative zero.
x-numeric-canonicalization.scope: These rules apply recursively to every deterministic value and key derivation, including nested observed values, evidence keys, candidate keys, validation evidence, acquisition facts, and export fields.

x-canonicalization-profile.name: PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1
x-canonicalization-profile.rules: Include only contract-declared deterministic fields and exclude operational UUIDs, timestamps, actors, UI/runtime state, storage paths, and transport metadata; NFC-preprocess strings; recursively order object keys by normalized project key rules; apply registered set-like and order-significant arrays; preserve every unregistered array as order-significant recursively; reject prohibited duplicates; distinguish null from absence; serialize UTF-8; use RFC 8785 number serialization; and encode exact lexical decimals with canonicalDecimalString.

x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.commonReplay: Every chain is append-only and same-subject. Ordinal 1 has no predecessor ID/content hash; each later ordinal increments exactly one and references the immediately preceding decision ID and recomputed deterministic content hash. Replay order is ordinal, never timestamp. Duplicate ordinals, gaps, branches, cycles, broken/stale predecessors, cross-subject links, invalid transitions, and superseding a non-effective decision are rejected.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.classificationApproval: Initial approve→approved or reject→rejected. approved→revoke→revoked or supersede→superseded; rejected→supersede→superseded; revoked→supersede→superseded. Rejection cannot be revoked; superseded is terminal for that proposal.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.relationshipDecision: Initial approve→approved or reject→rejected. approved→revoke→revoked or supersede→superseded; rejected→supersede→superseded; revoked→supersede→superseded. Rejection cannot be revoked; superseded is terminal for that relationship proposal.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.populationCandidateDecision: Initial approve→approved or reject→rejected. approved→revoke→revoked or supersede→superseded; rejected→supersede→superseded; revoked→supersede→superseded. Rejection cannot be revoked; superseded is terminal for that exact candidateKey and artifactSha256.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.quarantineDecision: Initial final-quarantine→final-quarantine, release→released, or reject→rejected. final-quarantine→continue-quarantine→final-quarantine, release→released, or supersede→superseded; released→revoke→revoked, inherit-release→released, or supersede→superseded; rejected→supersede→superseded; revoked→supersede→superseded. inherit-release requires the same unchanged artifact bytes and current effective release. Superseded is terminal.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.artifactEligibilityDecision: Initial approve→eligible, inherit-approval→eligible, or reject→rejected. Initial inherit-approval has no eligibility predecessor and requires a separate current-effective typed quarantine release ID/content hash for the same bytes. eligible→revoke→revoked or supersede→superseded; rejected→supersede→superseded; revoked→supersede→superseded. Later decisions use the ordinary eligibility predecessor chain. Superseded is terminal.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.authorityDecision: Initial approved or rejected. approved→revoked or superseded; rejected→superseded; revoked→superseded. Rejection cannot be revoked; superseded is terminal. Every noninitial record requires the immediately prior authority decision ID/content hash for the same proposal, classification approval, and artifact. Authority is effective only while the linked classification approval is the current effective same-artifact approval; its revocation, supersession, ineffectiveness, stale hash, or changed bytes immediately blocks dependent authority, and renewal requires a new valid typed authority decision.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.unresolvedItemDecision: Initial resolved or accepted-risk. resolved or accepted-risk→reopened; reopened→resolved, accepted-risk, or superseded; resolved or accepted-risk→superseded. Superseded is terminal; every noninitial record links to the immediately prior same-item decision.
x-complete-decision-transition-matrices.effectiveness: Approved, eligible, released, final-quarantine, rejected, resolved, and accepted-risk are effective only when they are the replay result of their valid chain. Revoked and superseded terminate the prior effective state; no timestamp changes effectiveness.
